notes.two_distinct_styles: Fall of Civilizations uses two thumbnail templates across 43 videos
notes.podcast_style: 17 videos use a consistent Thomas Cole painting ('The Course of Empire: Desolation') as background with 'FALL OF CIVILIZATIONS PODCAST' branding, episode number, and subtitle. These are the older/original uploads.
notes.episode_style: 25 videos use actual location photography (ruins, landscapes, archaeological sites) with 'EPISODE X' header, civilization name, and subtitle. These are the newer re-uploads that consistently outperform the podcast versions.
notes.one_exception: jpAphcaVJIs (Assyrians) uses an Assyrian stone relief carving as background rather than a landscape photo, classified as historical_photo.
notes.universal_traits: ALL 43 thumbnails have text overlay. ZERO have maps, faces, arrows, or icons. Every thumbnail is text_dominant in design but the background visual varies between artwork and landscape photography.
notes.text_pattern: Every thumbnail follows the same structure: episode number + civilization name + evocative subtitle. The text IS the thumbnail - no other visual hooks are used.
notes.no_faces_ever: Fall of Civilizations never shows the creator (Paul Cooper) or any human face in thumbnails. This is unusual for YouTube but consistent with their cinematic documentary brand.
notes.performance_correlation: The landscape/photography style thumbnails (newer uploads) consistently get more views than the painting-style podcast thumbnails for the same episodes, suggesting the switch to location photography improved CTR.
